title: Torsion coefficient assembly
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square],

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

with $f$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $g$ arbitrary, and let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], regarded as a complex concentrated in degree $0$, an object of $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then the derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]

$$
\Ex_{\square,F}:g^{-1}Rf_*F\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$. Equivalently, for every $p\in\mathbf Z$ the induced map of cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,F})$ is an isomorphism; through $\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}Rf_*F)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^p(Rf_*F)=g^{-1}R^pf_*F$ and $\mathcal H^p(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F)=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] this is the base change map $g^{-1}R^pf_*F\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}F$.

proof.text: **Step 0 (notation; reduction to cohomology sheaves).** Fix $\square$ with $f$ proper. Write $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $\Psi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$, functors $\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$, and $\Ex=\Ex_\square:\Phi\to\Psi$ for the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], natural in its argument. For an abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ (in degree $0$) say that $P(G)$ holds if $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_G):\mathcal H^p(\Phi G)\to\mathcal H^p(\Psi G)$ is an isomorphism for every $p\in\mathbf Z$. A morphism of $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ is an isomorphism if and only if it induces isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology]; so $\Ex_G$ is an isomorphism if and only if $P(G)$ holds, and the lemma (both of its formulations) says $P(F)$ for every torsion sheaf $F$. The identification $\mathcal H^p(\Phi G)\cong g^{-1}R^pf_*G$ in the statement is the natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}L)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^p(L)$ for the exact functor $g^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], applied to $L=Rf_*G$, together with $R^pf_*G=\mathcal H^p(Rf_*G)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (line 18360), proof, paragraph 1 (lines 18375-18384: 'We want to show the maps of sheaves $g^{-1}R^qf_*\mathcal F\to R^qf'_*(g')^{-1}\mathcal F$ are isomorphisms for all $q$')

proof.text: **Step 1 (prime coefficients; unit step 2).** Let $r$ be a prime and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ killed by $r$. Then multiplication by any integer on $G$ depends only on its class mod $r$, so $G$ is a sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules, and by the prime case of proper base change [lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change] (for the proper $f$ and the cartesian square $\square$) $\Ex_G$ is an isomorphism. Applying the functors $\mathcal H^p$ gives $P(G)$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (line 18360), proof, paragraph 3, last sentence ('In this way we reduce to the case that $\mathcal F$ is annihilated by a prime number $\ell$'), and paragraph 4; Theorem 095T (line 18610) proves that case

proof.text: **Step 2 (the devissage sequence).** Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ killed by $n=rn'$ with $r$ prime, and let $G[r]=\ker(r:G\to G)$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. In the abelian category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] the sequence $0\to G[r]\xrightarrow{i}G\xrightarrow{\pi}G/G[r]\to0$, with $i$ the kernel inclusion and $\pi$ its cokernel, is short exact. $G[r]$ is killed by $r$, since $r\circ i=0$ by definition of the kernel. $G/G[r]$ is killed by $n'$: the composite $G\xrightarrow{n'}G\xrightarrow{r}G$ is $n=0$, so $n':G\to G$ factors through $i$, hence $\pi\circ n'=0$; as $\pi$ is additive, $\pi\circ n'=n'\circ\pi$, and $\pi$ is an epimorphism, so $n'\cdot\mathrm{id}_{G/G[r]}=0$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives, line 18360), proof, paragraph 3 (lines 18403-18414), first two sentences

proof.text: **Step 3 (the exchange maps form a morphism of triangles).** The short exact sequence of Step 2 gives a distinguished triangle $G[r]\xrightarrow{i}G\xrightarrow{\pi}G/G[r]\xrightarrow{\delta}G[r][1]$ in $D(X_{\Et})$ [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle], all of whose vertices lie in the full triangulated subcategory $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], so it is distinguished there. The functor $\Phi$ is the composite of the triangulated functors $Rf_*$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] and $g^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] (triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]), and $\Psi$ the composite of $g'^{-1}$ and $Rf'_*$; a composite of triangulated functors is triangulated with the composite shift isomorphisms $\xi$, resp. $\zeta$. Hence $\Phi G[r]\to\Phi G\to\Phi(G/G[r])\xrightarrow{\xi\circ\Phi\delta}(\Phi G[r])[1]$ and $\Psi G[r]\to\Psi G\to\Psi(G/G[r])\xrightarrow{\zeta\circ\Psi\delta}(\Psi G[r])[1]$ are distinguished in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$, and by the compatibility of the exchange transformation with shifts and triangles [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated], part (2), the triple $(\Ex_{G[r]},\Ex_G,\Ex_{G/G[r]})$ is a morphism between these two triangles [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift].

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives, line 18360), proof, paragraph 3 (lines 18403-18414) ('the long exact sequence of higher direct images'; the long exact sequences are those of the triangles written here)

proof.text:
**Step 4 (five lemma).** In the situation of Step 3 assume $P(G[r])$ and $P(G/G[r])$. The two distinguished triangles have long exact cohomology sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], and the morphism of triangles of Step 3 makes $(\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{G[r]}),\mathcal H^p(\Ex_G),\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{G/G[r]}))_p$ a morphism between them, commuting also with the connecting maps [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder]. For each $p$, the five-term piece
$$\mathcal H^{p-1}(\Phi(G/G[r]))\to\mathcal H^p(\Phi G[r])\to\mathcal H^p(\Phi G)\to\mathcal H^p(\Phi(G/G[r]))\to\mathcal H^{p+1}(\Phi G[r])$$
and its $\Psi$-counterpart are exact rows, and the vertical maps $\mathcal H^{p-1}(\Ex_{G/G[r]})$, $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{G[r]})$, $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{G/G[r]})$, $\mathcal H^{p+1}(\Ex_{G[r]})$ are isomorphisms by hypothesis. By the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_G)$ is an isomorphism. Hence $P(G)$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives, line 18360), proof, paragraph 3 (lines 18403-18414) ('if the result holds for both $\mathcal F[\ell]$ and $\mathcal F/\mathcal F[\ell]$, then the result holds by the long exact sequence of higher direct images (and the 5 lemma)')

proof.text: **Step 5 (induction on the number of prime factors; unit step 3, first half).** For an integer $n\ge1$ let $\Omega(n)$ be the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. We show by induction on $\Omega(n)$ that $P(G)$ holds for every abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ killed by $n$. If $\Omega(n)=0$, then $n=1$ and $G=0$; $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are additive, so $\Phi G$ and $\Psi G$ are zero objects and $P(G)$ holds. If $\Omega(n)\ge1$, choose a prime $r\mid n$ and write $n=rn'$, so $\Omega(n')=\Omega(n)-1$. By Step 2, $G[r]$ is killed by $r$ and $G/G[r]$ by $n'$; $P(G[r])$ holds by Step 1 and $P(G/G[r])$ by the induction hypothesis; Step 4 gives $P(G)$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives, line 18360), proof, paragraph 3 (lines 18403-18414) ('In this way we reduce to the case that $\mathcal F$ is annihilated by a prime number $\ell$')

proof.text: **Step 6 (the source side commutes with the colimit).** Let $F$ be a torsion sheaf on $X_{\Et}$: by definition [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] the canonical map $c_F:\varinjlim_nF[n]\to F$, the colimit taken over the positive integers ordered by divisibility (a directed set), is an isomorphism; let $\iota_n:F[n]\hookrightarrow F$ be the inclusions. The morphism $f$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Each $F[n]$ is killed by $n$, so every local section of it is killed by $n$ and $(F[n])_n$ is a filtered system of torsion sheaves in the sense of [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit], which gives that $\varinjlim_nR^pf_*F[n]\to R^pf_*(\varinjlim_nF[n])$ is an isomorphism for every $p\ge0$ (for $p<0$ all terms are $0$). Composing with $R^pf_*(c_F)$, the map $\varinjlim_nR^pf_*F[n]\to R^pf_*F$ induced by the $R^pf_*\iota_n$ is an isomorphism. Applying $g^{-1}$, which commutes with colimits [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], the map $\varinjlim_ng^{-1}R^pf_*F[n]\to g^{-1}R^pf_*F$ induced by the $g^{-1}R^pf_*\iota_n$ is an isomorphism. Through the isomorphisms $\mathcal H^p(\Phi G)\cong g^{-1}R^pf_*G$ of Step 0, which are natural in $G$, this says: the map $a_p:\varinjlim_n\mathcal H^p(\Phi F[n])\to\mathcal H^p(\Phi F)$ induced by the $\mathcal H^p(\Phi\iota_n)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives, line 18360), proof, paragraph 2 (lines 18386-18400); Lemma 09Z1 (lemma-relative-colimit, line 7535) is the commutation of $R^pf_*$ with filtered colimits for $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, here applied with the constant system of schemes

proof.text: **Step 7 (the target side commutes with the colimit).** The base change $f'$ of the proper morphism $f$ along $g$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Since $g'^{-1}$ commutes with colimits [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], the map $\varinjlim_ng'^{-1}F[n]\to g'^{-1}F$ induced by the $g'^{-1}\iota_n$ is the isomorphism $g'^{-1}(c_F)$ composed with that canonical isomorphism. Each $g'^{-1}F[n]$ is killed by $n$ ($g'^{-1}$ is additive, so it carries multiplication by $n$, which is $0$ on $F[n]$, to multiplication by $n$), hence is torsion, and [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] for $f'$ gives that $\varinjlim_nR^pf'_*g'^{-1}F[n]\to R^pf'_*(\varinjlim_ng'^{-1}F[n])$ is an isomorphism. Composing, and using $\mathcal H^p(\Psi G)=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the map $b_p:\varinjlim_n\mathcal H^p(\Psi F[n])\to\mathcal H^p(\Psi F)$ induced by the $\mathcal H^p(\Psi\iota_n)$ is an isomorphism for every $p$.

**Step 8 (passage to the colimit; conclusion).** By naturality of $\Ex$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], for every $n$ one has $\Ex_F\circ\Phi\iota_n=\Psi\iota_n\circ\Ex_{F[n]}$, and likewise for the inclusions $F[n]\hookrightarrow F[m]$, $n\mid m$; applying $\mathcal H^p$, the maps $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{F[n]})$ form a morphism of filtered diagrams $(\mathcal H^p(\Phi F[n]))_n\to(\mathcal H^p(\Psi F[n]))_n$ and $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_F)\circ a_p=b_p\circ\varinjlim_n\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{F[n]})$. Each $F[n]$ is killed by $n$, so $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{F[n]})$ is an isomorphism by Step 5; a morphism of diagrams whose components are isomorphisms has an inverse morphism of diagrams, so $\varinjlim_n\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{F[n]})$ is an isomorphism. As $a_p$ (Step 6) and $b_p$ (Step 7) are isomorphisms, so is $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_F)$, for every $p$. This is $P(F)$, and by Step 0 $\Ex_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives, line 18360), proof, paragraph 2 (lines 18386-18400) ('Hence we see that $g^{-1}R^qf_*\mathcal F=\colim g^{-1}R^qf_*\mathcal F[n]$ and $R^qf'_*(g')^{-1}\mathcal F=\colim R^qf'_*(g')^{-1}\mathcal F[n]$. Thus it suffices to prove the result in case $\mathcal F$ is annihilated by a positive integer $n$'); the compatibility of the identifications with the base change maps, left implicit there, is the naturality used here

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ and every proper Cartesian square, the
specific map $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Write $F=\varinjlim_nF[n]$ and commute both sides of exchange with the
filtered colimit. Induct on the number of prime factors of $n$ through
$0\to F[\ell]\to F[n]\to F[n]/F[\ell]\to0$; the quotient is killed by
$n/\ell$. Prime coefficients are handled by the preceding lemma, and the
five-lemma transfer handles the induction step. Naturality shows at every
stage that the comparison is the S0 exchange map.

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** The route above reaches the statement for every proper $f$:
neither [lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change] nor the reduction
[prop-weil-pbc-reduction-to-projective-line] carries a finite-presentation
hypothesis, since the Chow lemma [lemma-weil-pbc-chow-factorization] used in
the reduction is proved for every proper morphism over an affine base. For the
general proper morphism the classical statement is Etale Cohomology,
Theorem 59.91.11 (Tag [095T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095T)):
"Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes. Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism
of schemes ... Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian torsion sheaf on
$X_{\acute{e}tale}$. Then the base change map $g^{-1}Rf_*\mathcal{F}\to
Rf'_*(g')^{-1}\mathcal{F}$ is an isomorphism." Its proof follows the same
route as the one above: the reduction to $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ for every
scheme $S$ is Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.91.10 (Tag
[0A4F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A4F)), and the strictly henselian
computation is the comparison $\Gamma(X,\mathcal{F})=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal{F}|_Z)$
of Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag [0A0B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A0B)), which
Stacks derives from Stein factorization (More on Morphisms, Theorem 37.53.5,
Tag [03H2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03H2)) and henselian
idempotent lifting (More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.8, Tag
[09XK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XK)). Accordingly the only
inputs of this route that the chapter does not supply are the two Stein
inputs [thm-weil-pbc-stein-inputs]; they are supplied in the literature by
the chain just named, and closing them here means decomposing that chain.
